title: Benchmark report visual system (charts + PDF/web consistency + accessibility)
creator: Talia Benson
description:
Goal
Define a reusable visual system for the public-facing “Latency per dollar” benchmark report that stays consistent across:
- Web landing page (redwood.ai / docs site)
- Downloadable PDF report
- Embedded charts in blog post / docs appendix

This ticket covers: chart style rules, color palette, typography, layout grid, and accessibility requirements, plus handoff artifacts for Marketing + Docs engineering.

Context
We’re publishing performance/cost benchmarks across model families and regions. The visuals must communicate “production economics” clearly without over-claiming and must remain readable when:
- printed (PDF)
- viewed on mobile (web)
- seen in grayscale (screenshots, printouts)
- interpreted by colorblind users

Non-goals
- Creating every final chart (covered by chart production + page build work)
- Selecting the headline stats or claims language

Owners / collaborators
- Design lead: Tessa Morgan
- Chart/page design: Alicia Perez
- Narrative/marketing: Ethan Wallace, Soojin Lee
- Docs/web: Elliot Price, Wei Chen

Deliverables (what “done” means)
1) Figma library for the benchmark report
- Color styles (named tokens)
- Text styles (web + PDF)
- Chart primitives (axes, gridlines, legend, annotations)
- Components: bar chart, line chart, scatter plot, table, callout, footnote/disclaimer block

2) “Benchmark Visual System” guidelines doc (1–2 pages)
- Chart rules + do/don’t examples
- Accessibility rules + QA checklist
- Export guidance (PNG/SVG/PDF)

3) Handoff package to Docs engineering + Marketing
- Token list (hex values + usage)
- Type scale (px and pt)
- Spacing/grid rules
- Chart annotation standard (variance bands, footnotes, region tags)


Visual system specification

A) Color palette (accessible + print-aware)
Principles
- Meet WCAG 2.1 AA contrast for text and key UI elements.
- Don’t rely on red/green distinctions.
- Use color to group “model family” and use shape/annotation to convey “region” where needed.
- Charts must remain interpretable in grayscale: use line styles, markers, or labels for secondary differentiation.

Core tokens (names + intended usage)
- Redwood Ink (#0B1220): primary text, axes labels
- Redwood Slate (#344054): secondary text
- Redwood Mist (#D0D5DD): gridlines, dividers
- Redwood Paper (#FFFFFF): background
- Redwood Teal (#10B981): primary highlight/Redwood emphasis (use sparingly; not for every series)
- Redwood Blue (#2563EB): secondary series
- Redwood Violet (#7C3AED): secondary series
- Redwood Amber (#F59E0B): caution/notes (never for “bad performance” semantics)
- Redwood Red (#DC2626): reserved only for errors/outages, not benchmark comparisons

Model-family series palette (for charts with multiple families)
- Family A: Blue
- Family B: Violet
- Family C: Teal
- Family D: Neutral Slate (only when needed)
Guidance: max 4 concurrent series in one chart; otherwise use small multiples.

Region mapping (avoid “too many colors”)
- Prefer labels (US-East, US-West, EU-Central, APAC) + subtle tags.
- If regions must be encoded, use marker shapes:
  - US: circle
  - EU: square
  - APAC: triangle

Contrast requirements
- Body text on Paper: 4.5:1 minimum
- Axis labels/legend text: 4.5:1 minimum
- Gridlines: may be lower contrast but must not compete with data; target ~10–15% opacity Ink/Mist equivalent


B) Typography (web + PDF)
Font stack
- Primary: Inter (web + PDF)
- Monospace (code/config snippets): IBM Plex Mono (or ui-monospace fallback for web)

Type scale (Web)
- H1: 40/48, weight 700
- H2: 28/36, weight 700
- H3: 20/28, weight 600
- Body: 16/24, weight 400
- Small/Caption: 13/18, weight 400
- Footnote/Disclaimer: 12/18, weight 400

Type scale (PDF)
- Title: 26 pt / 32 pt, 700
- Section header: 16 pt / 22 pt, 700
- Subheader: 12 pt / 18 pt, 600
- Body: 10.5 pt / 15 pt, 400 (minimum 10 pt)
- Caption: 9.5 pt / 13 pt, 400 (use sparingly)
- Footnote/Disclosure: 9 pt / 12 pt, 400

Numeric formatting
- Use tabular numbers where possible (Figma setting / CSS font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums).
- Units must be explicit (ms, tokens/s, $/1M tokens, latency/$).


C) Chart styling rules

Default chart canvas
- Background: Paper
- Plot border: none
- Gridlines: horizontal only by default; vertical only when necessary (e.g., time series)
- Axes: Ink at 60–70% opacity equivalent (lighter than body text)

Data ink hierarchy
1) Data series / bars
2) Annotations (p95 callouts, variance bands, “best-in-region” labels)
3) Axes labels
4) Gridlines

Line charts
- Stroke: 2 px (web) / 1.25 pt (PDF)
- Markers: enabled when multiple regions are present; 4 px web / 2.5 pt PDF
- If showing confidence/variance: use band fill at ~15% opacity, same hue as line; include legend label “run-to-run variance”

Bar charts
- Corner radius: 4 px (web) / 2 pt (PDF)
- Spacing: 8 px within group, 16 px between groups
- Always include value labels if the chart will be used as a standalone social image

Scatter plots (latency vs cost, latency/$)
- Use x/y axis titles with units
- Use marker shapes for region; color for model family
- Add trendline only if methodology team approves; otherwise omit to avoid implying causality

Tables (for PDF appendix and web)
- Zebra striping: Mist at 6–8% opacity
- Right-align numeric columns
- Include “Last updated” and “Methodology version” row in footer for reproducibility

Annotations & footnotes
- Standard annotation pattern: small superscript marker (1, 2, 3) + footnote block below chart
- Standard disclaimer block component (used across web/PDF): “Benchmarks are workload-dependent…” language placeholder; final text owned by Marketing + Legal


D) Layout, spacing, export guidance
Spacing
- 8-pt grid for all chart and page layouts
- Minimum spacing between chart and caption: 12 px web / 8 pt PDF

PDF page layout
- Page size: US Letter (primary) with A4 compatibility (avoid edge-to-edge elements)
- Margins: 0.75 in minimum
- Charts should not be narrower than 5.8 in in the PDF content area to preserve legibility

Export formats
- Web: SVG preferred for charts; PNG fallback at 2x for complex raster elements
- PDF: vector charts when possible; otherwise 300 DPI PNG
- Social: 1200x627 and 1080x1080 templates (covered in DES-232)


Accessibility requirements + QA checklist
- Contrast: verify key text and data encodings meet WCAG AA on Paper background.
- Colorblind safety: run quick check (deuteranopia/protanopia) on multi-series charts; ensure marker shapes or direct labels are present.
- Minimum font size: 10 pt (PDF) / 13 px (web) for critical chart labels.
- Avoid encoding meaning solely by color (e.g., “good vs bad”).
- Alt text: every chart on the landing page must have alt text that states:
  1) what is being compared (models/regions)
  2) what metric (latency/$, p50/p95)
  3) key takeaway (non-superlative, factual)
- Focus states (web): any interactive filters/toggles must have visible focus outline and keyboard navigation.


Links / artifacts
- Figma file (library + components): https://figma.com/file/REDACTED/benchmark-visual-system
- Draft chart spec (inputs from Marketing): sources/google_drive/shared_drives/go-to-market/benchmark-report-charts-spec.json
- Landing page wirecopy (for layout alignment): sources/google_drive/shared_drives/go-to-market/benchmark-report-landing-page-wirecopy.json


Open questions (resolved in comments)
- Whether to use model-family colors consistently across all assets vs per-chart optimization.
- Whether region should be encoded by color at all (decision: prefer shape + label; limited use of color tags).

Acceptance criteria
- Tokens are documented with names and exact values.
- At least 3 representative chart templates exist in Figma (bar, line, scatter) with correct axis/legend/caption styles.
- Accessibility checklist exists and is referenced by Docs/Web implementers.
- Marketing and Docs sign off that the system is usable for the report and landing page.
comments: 2025-01-16 (Alicia Perez): Drafted initial palette mapping for model families. Proposed keeping Teal as “Redwood highlight” only; avoid Teal for an entire family to prevent everything looking like “Redwood wins.”

2025-01-18 (Soojin Lee): +1 to avoiding implied superiority through color. Please ensure the same chart can be screenshot into a competitor comparison without us looking like we’re styling ourselves as the default “best.”
2025-01-22 (Ethan Wallace): Request: add a standard disclaimer/citation block component that we can drop under every chart in the PDF. Legal wants consistent placement.
2025-01-24 (Wei Chen): For docs site, we’ll likely render charts as SVG/PNG. Can you provide minimum label sizes and a recommendation for when to force value labels on bars (mobile readability)?
2025-01-28 (Tessa Morgan): Added mobile rules: if chart width < 360px, use simplified legend or direct labels and reduce series count. Added tabular number guidance for metric tables.
2025-02-03 (Elliot Price): Handoff received. We can map tokens into CSS variables; request final list in a copy/paste-friendly format (name -> hex) for implementation.
